text:
support_alex: Heads up — customer GloboPay on Dedicated reported sudden throttling and auth 429s during long-context invoices flow. They see sharp latency spikes and a stream of cache-evict log lines. Opened ticket #GLB-432.

customer_ops_tim: Pasting the anonymized tail of the instance logs we captured (timestamped around the spike):

```
[2026-03-16T14:02:11Z] tenant=glb-prod evict_rate=342 evicted_keys=1205 kv_free=18% kv_frag=0.62 ctx_len=17408 inflight=24
[2026-03-16T14:02:12Z] tenant=glb-prod warn: long_context_detected seq_len=17200 model=redwood-3b quant=8bit
[2026-03-16T14:02:12Z] tenant=glb-prod evict: dropping prefix-cache entries=48 reason=memory_pressure
[2026-03-16T14:02:13Z] tenant=glb-prod throttle: responses 429 route=/v1/generate queue_depth=18
```

support_alex: Repro steps from customer: 1) open convo with ~12k tokens historic, 2) append 6k token prompt delta, 3) call /v1/chat/stream concurrently from 6 clients. They started seeing 429s after ~30s and throughput collapse.

eng_runtime_jess: Thanks — couple quick Qs: which model variant (fp16/8bit), and is this on Dedicated with shared host (multi-tenant pool) or reserved node? Also, did they recently change autoscale/min_replicas?

customer_ops_tim: They're on Dedicated shared pool (reserved capacity but multi-tenant), model pinned to redwood-3b-quant8. No policy change on their side; we did run a config rollout to change autoscaler cooldown on 2026-03-16 13:58 (small window).

eng_sre_mike: Noted. The logs look like KV cache churn + fragmentation causing lots of evictions which increases request tail latency and then our QoS throttles the tenant to protect node SLOs. Can you grab the per-tenant kv metrics (kv_hits, kv_misses, kv_fragmentation) for the last 10m? Also need tenant's concurrency and sequence length distribution.

support_alex: Attached metrics snapshot from CloudWatch (sent privately). Key points: kv_hits dropped from 0.91 to 0.57; kv_frag jumped from 0.31 to 0.62; avg_seq_len moved from 8k to 15k. Concurrency peaked at 22.

eng_runtime_jess: That's consistent with fragmentation causing the cache allocator to fail fast at the tail. Two-pronged plan: short-term mitigation and a repro/patch path. Short term: 1) ask customer to temporarily reduce concurrency to <=8 or enable their canary that truncates historical context; 2) on our side increase tenant cache quota on their Dedicated pool (manual bump) and temporarily relax per-tenant throttle thresholds for glb-prod so we can collect traces without killing requests.

eng_sre_mike: I'll prepare the manual cache bump script. Also rolling back the autoscaler cooldown tweak might help because the autoscaler delayed adding capacity during the ramp. deploy-bot: did the autoscaler cooldown change we rolled out at 13:58 affect this pool?

deploy-bot: autoscaler:policy: "dedicated-default" applied to pool: shard-9 at 2026-03-16T13:58:02 by eng_platform_rollback. Change: cooldown from 45s -> 180s.

eng_runtime_jess: That's likely the smoking gun — cooldown increase means we didn't spin up extra workers under sustained heavy long-context requests, so KV pressure built up. eng_platform needs to revert or tune the cooldown for long-context-heavy tenants.

support_alex: Customer asked if this is billable — they lost throughput for ~12 minutes and saw 429s. billing_kate: any notes?

billing_kate: We'll treat this as a service incident review. If we determine platform config change caused degraded SLA, support should file a credit request path; hold off final billing adjustments until postmortem.

eng_sre_mike: Immediate actions I'm taking: 1) run manual cache-quota bump for glb-prod on shard-9 (10% extra) 2) revert autoscaler cooldown on shard-9 to 45s 3) add a temporary cache-frag alert (kv_frag > 0.55 for 5m) to catch recurrence. I'll document commands in the incident doc.

eng_runtime_jess: For repro/work item: we need a small deterministic repro harness to simulate long-context churn: script will open N sessions with initial history ~12k tokens, then append a 4-6k token delta and stream concurrently. Please try with concurrency 12/16/24 and capture per-token latency + kv allocator traces. I can work on a minimal curl/js harness.

customer_ops_tim: We're willing to run the harness with a test tenant. We can also short-term switch some heavy customers to a model with lower KV footprint.

support_alex: Action items assigned: eng_sre_mike (manual bump + revert cooldown) eng_runtime_jess (repro harness + allocator traces) support_alex (coordinate customer mitigations + credit path) eng_platform (confirm permanent autoscaler policy update). Meeting in 30m to sync. :thumbsup:

eng_sre_mike: Update — manual bump executed at 14:06 UTC, cache usage stabilized and 429s dropped within 90s. Rolling cooldown revert now.

eng_runtime_jess: I'll start the repro harness and paste commands. Example repro curl (anonymized):

```
curl -s -N -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.test/v1/chat/stream \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TEST_KEY}" \
 -d '{"model":"redwood-3b-quant8","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<12k tokens of history>"}],"max_tokens":6000}'
```

support_alex: Thanks everyone. We'll escalate to a postmortem if eng_platform confirms the cooldown change caused the capacity lag. For now customer reporting recovered.

billing_kate: Marking ticket GLB-432 as L1 incident pending postmortem.

eng_runtime_jess: Perf note for follow-up: long-context workloads amplify allocator fragmentation. Long-term fixes: compacting allocator, background defrag pass, or per-tenant slab isolation on Dedicated pools. I'll draft RFC items after repro results.

support_alex: Closing loop — customer confirmed normal operations at 14:09 UTC. We'll keep the alert in place for 24 hours. :white_check_mark:
